meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (Republic of Panama) - unitary national jurisdiction with no sub-state tax distinction
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic tradition, supplemented by the Private Interest Foundation statutory regime modeled on Liechtenstein foundation law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama-United States Trade Promotion Agreement, in force 31 October 2012
Dominican Republic-Central America-United States Free Trade Agreement, effective for Panama 24 October 2013
Panama-China Bilateral Investment Treaty, signed 17 November 2017
Panama-Netherlands Double Taxation Agreement, signed 2019 and in force 2021
Panama-United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement, signed 2019 and in force 2020; Panama-United Kingdom Investment Protection Agreement of 1985

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Law) and its regulatory norms; Articles 4-14 covering constitution, registration, foundation council, resident agent, and fiscal obligations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Dirección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Public Registry of Panama, Private Interest Foundations Directorate)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado (Foundation Charter Deed) followed by annotation in the Folio Real.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Panama Law 25 of 1995 sets no mandatory paid-up capital amount, but the Foundation Charter must state the initial endowment (patrimonio inicial). Standard notarial and registry practice requires a stated initial endowment of at least USD 10,000 to evidence sufficient patrimony; no escrow deposit is mandated and the endowment is simply declared subscribed and received.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the founder hereby subscribes and confirms receipt of the initial endowment of the Foundation, as stated in the Foundation Charter, to be applied solely to the Foundation's lawful purposes under Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office is fixed at [Address], Panama City, Republic of Panama, and [Resident Agent Name] is appointed Resident Agent of the Foundation as required by Panamanian law. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [name/names] is/are appointed as members of the Foundation Council and [Name] as President and [Name] as Secretary thereof, each with full authority to open bank accounts, adopt the foundation regulations, and execute all documents required for statutory registration, tax filing, and industrial licensing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Search and Drafting of Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (name search booth / Sede Electrónica) and Notary Public of the Circuit of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an availability search for the proposed foundation name; upon clearance, instruct Panamanian counsel to prepare the Spanish Foundation Charter (Escritura Constitutiva) naming the foundation, initial endowment, purpose (ISIC 1079 instant rice noodle manufacturing), registered office, resident agent, foundation council members, and purpose restrictions.
required_dossiers: Proposed name variants (minimum three)
Certified copy of passport or ID of each founder and council member
Declaration of lawful origin of the initial endowment
Draft Foundation Charter in Spanish prepared by licensed counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is registered or reserved by another entity, re-submit with the next available variant, or file a Registry action to cancel an obsolete name (then wait 24 hours).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization and Execution of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Circuit of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Founders and foundation council members sign the Foundation Charter before a Panamanian notary, or through valid powers of attorney; the notary authenticates the deed and issues the testimonio and certification; pay notarial fees, fiscal stamps (timbre fiscal), and municipal visibility stamp (timbre municipal).
required_dossiers: Passports/ID cards of all signatories
Notarized power of attorney (if any party is absent)
Ready-to-sign Spanish charter in triplicate
Fiscal/municipal stamps receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a notarial defect is detected, cure by executing an addendum deed (addenda de corrección) before the same notary before presentation to the Public Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Foundation with the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Dirección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (digital filing via Tu Registro portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarial testimonio together with the registration application and fee payment (approx. USD 250) in the electronic petition system; the Registry opens a Folio Real record and issues the Certificado de Registro y Personería Jurídica evidencing legal personality.
required_dossiers: Notarial testimonio of the Foundation Charter
Completed foundation registration form (solicitud)
Proof of payment of registration fee and stamps
Power of attorney of the presenting attorney (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry files a reparo (office action), file a written response within three business days; if denied, appeal to the Director General or seek judicial challenging via the civil circuit court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and Social Security Registration (RUC and CSS Employer Account)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) - Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Caja de Seguro Social (CSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the foundation in the Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) to obtain the taxpayer ID and activate the DGI Sede Electrónica for monthly ISR/ITBMS filings; if employees will be hired, register the foundation as employer with CSS and obtain the employer quota codes.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Registro y Personería Jurídica
Foundation Charter
ID of the President of the Foundation Council
Proof of registered office address
RUC registration form (formulario de inscripción)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI questions the address or purpose, re-file with a lease agreement and municipal aviso; request expedited review at the DGI taxpayer assistance office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Aviso de Operación for the Noodle Manufacturing Plant
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipio de Panamá - Dirección de Rentas Municipales
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the municipal establishment license (Aviso de Operación) for the manufacturing premises, pay the annual municipal patent fee determined from projected gross receipts, undergo the officials' inspection, and physically post the aviso at the factory.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate
Lease agreement or title of premises
Zoning/uso de suelo certificate
Fire safety certificate issued by the fire department
Council resolution appointing legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If aviso is denied based on zoning, procure the cambio de uso de suelo (change of land use) from the Municipal Engineering Directorate and re-submit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) - Dirección de Alimentos y Bebidas; Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) - Dirección Nacional de Empresas (Industrial Registry)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registro Sanitario de Alimentos (Food Sanitary Registration) and Aviso de Operación Industrial (Industrial Establishment Operation Notice)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) - Dirección Nacional de Evaluación y Seguimiento Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoría I - Declaración de Impacto Ambiental for small-to-medium food processing plants; upgrade to Categoría II - Estudio de Impacto Ambiental Simplificado where daily rice noodle output or wastewater discharge exceeds MiAMBIENTE thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must comply with Decreto Ejecutivo No. 12 de 2018 and MiAMBIENTE Resolución AG-0113-2000: pH 6.5-8.5; BOD5 ≤ 100 mg/L; TSS ≤ 100 mg/L; COD ≤ 250 mg/L; total residual chlorine ≤ 0.5 mg/L; no visible grease or floatable matter; solid organic waste (rice flour, spent broths) must be segregated and disposed under Law No. 33 of 2018; VOC/particulate emissions from frying and retort lines must respect workplace exposure limits under MINSA/MITRADEL norms.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de la República de Panamá based on extinguishers, sprinkler design, and evacuation routes; structural load inspection and occupational safety authorization by the Municipal Engineering Directorate; workplace health clearance from MINSA with a written occupational risk prevention plan (Sistema de Gestión de Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo) approved by MITRADEL.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama. Principal digital portals: e-Tax (https://e-tax.dgi.gob.pa); the Sistema Integrado de Facturación Electrónica (SIE) for mandatory electronic invoicing; Panamá Emprende for the one-stop business registration window; and the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) via the SICE customs declaration platform for export controls.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: STEP 1 — Entity formation: a foreign founder executes and registers the Private Interest Foundation (PIF) charter before the Registro Público de Panamá through a Panamanian resident attorney, appointing a resident agent and defining the foundation's patrimony, council, and purposes. STEP 2 — Operating licence: file the Aviso de Operación with the competent municipality (through Panamá Emprende or the municipal treasury) and obtain the municipal operating permit for the instant-noodle manufacturing plant. STEP 3 — Statutory TIN/VAT ID (RUC): access the DGI e-Tax portal and complete the RUC application (Form 400 series), attaching the notarised foundation charter, resident-agent appointment, identification of foundation council members, and proof of the local registered address; the DGI issues a single RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) covering income tax, ITBMS, and employer obligations. STEP 4 — ITBMS and SIE activation: elect the monthly or quarterly ITBMS remittance profile in the RUC file, obtain a qualified digital-signature certificate from an AIG-accredited certification provider, and activate the SIE electronic-invoicing account. STEP 5 — Exporter registration: enrol with ANA to receive the customs exporter code and SICE access, and obtain the MINSA food-export sanitary registration for the retort-packaged rice-noodle products. Foreign entities with no Panama-source activity are not required to hold a RUC; however, any entity commencing manufacturing, importing, or domestic sales in Panama must complete registration before the first taxable transaction.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope — the Republic of Panama taxes income only where the source is located in Panama (Código Fiscal, Article 694). A Private Interest Foundation (Law 25 of 1995) is a separate juridical person and is treated as an entity-level taxpayer, not as a pass-through vehicle; it is taxable on Panama-source income at the general 25% corporate rate while foreign-source dividends, interest, royalties, and capital gains remain outside the Panamanian tax net. If the PIF acts purely as a holding structure with foreign-source revenue, its effective exposure to Panamanian income tax is nil. If the PIF itself operates the noodle factory in Panama, the DGI will attribute the manufacturing profit as Panama-source income taxable at entity level notwithstanding the foundation form.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not provide a US-style check-the-box election nor OECD hybrid-mismatch elections; entity classification follows the legal-character rules of the Código Fiscal and the foundation charter. Available statutory elections of tax relevance: (1) Small-taxpayer simplification — an eligible enterprise with annual gross turnover not exceeding the statutory ceiling may elect the 'pequeño contribuyente' regime, which simplifies ITBMS remittance and electronic-invoicing duties without removing the registration obligation. (2) Investment incentive contracts — a manufacturer may apply to elect a special fiscal stabilisation or strategic-investment regime (e.g., Law 41/2007 incentives, Panama Pacifico special economic zone, free-zone or export-processing-zone status), which modifies the effective income-tax and ITBMS burden. (3) Advance tax ruling or APA — a taxpayer may elect to submit a formal consultation to DGI to obtain a binding interpretation confirming the foreign-source versus Panama-source character of cross-border royalty, technical-assistance, or commission income flowing through the PIF. (4) Distribution timing election — the PIF council may elect when and whether to declare distributions from Panama-source profits, thereby determining the moment at which the 10% Panamanian dividend withholding tax becomes payable; distributions funded exclusively from foreign-source foundation patrimony are outside the Panamanian dividend tax. (5) No fiscal-unity or group-consolidation election exists; each juridical person files separately, and taxpayers may elect to structure the factory as a branch of the PIF or as a separate Panamanian subsidiary, with consequent differences in registration and territorial attribution.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP); Banco Nacional de Panamá serves as fiscal agent. Panama has no central bank and has adopted the US dollar as legal tender under Decree Law of 1904 and subsequent monetary arrangements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates a fully dollarized and open-currency economy. Both capital and current account transactions are freely convertible into USD without central bank exchange controls. Profit remittances from a Panamanian Private Interest Foundation are not blocked and are generally treated as foreign-source or foundation distributions outside Panama's territorial tax net, provided the underlying activity is carried on abroad and the funds are not derived from Panama-situs sources. Practical remittance frictions are limited to anti-money-laundering (AML) and tax-information obligations rather than exchange-rate surrender rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export proceeds surrender requirements in Panama. No mandated conversion ratio, no repatriation timeline, and no obligation to deposit export receipts into a monitored exchange account apply to the jurisdiction. Export proceeds of the instant rice noodle manufacturing business may be retained in USD, remitted to any authorized bank account, or freely used for trade settlement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Current/Chequing) and auxiliary USD collection account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account under single commercial banking relationship
Operational Account with integrated trade finance and SWIFT LC services
Cross-border USD settlement and treasury account; Capital Escrow Account if requested
Operational Account for foundation treasury, corporate cards, and e-banking

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium. Panama does not yet maintain a dedicated electronic money institution (EMI) license that confers direct clearing access. Digital cross-border fintech operators must either partner with a licensed Panamanian bank or obtain approval as a payment service provider under SBP fintech sandbox/innovation rules. Pure offshore EMIs without a local SBP-authorized presence are not viable as primary treasury raisers and carry enhanced AML due-diligence friction for the instant noodle manufacturer.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Most tier-1 Panamanian banks require at least one natural-person signatory, board member, or duly appointed attorney-in-fact to appear in person at account opening or branch activation. Remote/video-based KYC is increasingly accepted for low-risk food manufacturing clients after initial documentary review, but in-person verification remains the dominant compliance practice for Private Interest Foundation accounts. The PIF must ensure the Foundation Council appoints an authorized representative resident or physically available in Panama.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear or undisclosed economic settlor / final beneficiary of the Private Interest Foundation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Private Interest Foundation charter and Foundation Council appointment minutes, apostilled or legalized, plus a written effective-beneficial-owner declaration identifying the economic settlor and any designated beneficiaries, supported by passport copies, utility/proof of address, and a notarized source-of-wealth statement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore capital injection from a jurisdiction considered high-risk or non-cooperative for tax purposes
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Categorized wire instructions with complete remitter-beneficiary infrastructure, source-of-funds letter, bank statements for the sending entity, commercial agreement or board resolution approving the funding, and evidence of the underlying factory/operating assets supporting the instant rice noodle project.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade payment red flags relating to cross-border import of specialty ingredients or packaging from China
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full PDF set of purchase orders, commercial invoices, bills of lading, packing lists, customs filings in Panama and export-country, tariff classification certificate, product labelling/sanitary registration under Panama's Ministry of Health (MINSA), and counterparty KYC dossier confirming no OFAC/EU/UN sanction exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Low operational substance due to PIF structure with no physical office or payroll records
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease agreement for a Panamanian registered office or warehouse, local correspondent contact or administrator appointment, payroll listing and social-security filings for any Panama-based staff, equipment inventory, and a notarized operational overview detailing manufacturing, warehousing, logistics, and sales activities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Passage of funds through a PAN-PIF account without clear redistribution or dividend policy
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foundation council resolutions articulating treasury policy, planned distributions or reinvestment, audited trial balance or interim financial statements, supporting invoice trail for all operating expenditures, and tax opinion confirming the territorial-source treatment of international trading income.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections are routed over SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 for interbank bulk credits) through the PIF's USD correspondent clearing channel into the Panamanian beneficiary account. Panama does not maintain a formal FX purpose-code table; banks use standard SWIFT Purpose/Category fields to evidence the transaction. The recommended payment narrative is 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION TO PRIVATE INTEREST FOUNDATION – INSTANT RICE NOODLE MANUFACTURING PROJECT' together with a board resolution or capital call notice. Verification is completed by the receiving bank via anti-money-laundering profiling, match against the KYC file, and documentation of the remitter account and underlying commercial activity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound supplier and logistics payments are settled via SWIFT MT103 wire transfer in USD, or through commercial letters of credit (LC) for larger ingredient purchases and plant equipment. The principal clearing rails are the SBP-regulated local banks' USD nostro channels via Fedwire/CHIPS, with a SWIFT-correspondent chain. Immediate rice noodle manufacturing disbursements should use irrevocable sight/term LCs with beneficiary-presented documents or T/T prepayment against verified invoices. All documentary credits must conform to UCP600 rules and include commodity-detail fields compliant with OFAC screening and Panamanian AML reporting obligations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/EUR and USD/CNY deliverable forward contracts with SBP-authorized commercial banks under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement
USD/CNH non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) transacted offshore for hedging Chinese RMB-based raw-material costs
Cross-currency swaps between USD and EUR or CNY arranged with tier-1 counterparties for large capex repayment hedging
Plain vanilla USD/EUR currency options for negotiated import settlements
Commodity-linked hedging contracts on rice and edible-oil inputs permitted through licensed brokerage/treasury operations for margin stability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Tax (Impuesto Anual de Personas Jurídicas / Tasa Anual de Mantenimiento)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) and Registro Público de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before June 30; for newly registered Private Interest Foundations, the first annual payment is due by June 30 of the first full calendar year of registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment incurs statutory surcharges and may suspend issuance of the good-standing certificate; persistent non-payment for more than one year, after formal notice, may trigger administrative strike-off of the foundation's registration from the Registro Público.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Registry Confirmation / Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Beneficial Ownership Registry (Registro de Titulares de Beneficio Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No fixed filing deadline for unchanged ownership; updates must be filed within 30 calendar days of any beneficial ownership or foundation council change. An annual confirmation to the resident agent is required in connection with the June 30 maintenance cycle.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to keep the Beneficial Ownership Registry current constitutes an administrative infraction; penalties may include fines, suspension of the foundation's good-standing certificate, and, in cases of serious or repeated non-compliance, administrative strike-off after formal notice.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory independent statutory audit is imposed on a non-commercial Private Interest Foundation under Law 25 of 1995. An audit becomes compulsory only if the foundation's charter or bylaws require it, if the foundation carries on regulated commercial activities in Panama, or if consolidated tax or financial regulatory obligations apply through an underlying operating entity.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS / NIIF as adopted in Panama for entities with statutory accounting obligations; a non-operating PIF is not required to file audited financial statements with the Registro Público.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Private Interest Foundations have no share capital. The resident agent must annually confirm the identities of the founder, foundation council members, protector (if appointed), and beneficiaries. Any change in beneficial interest or council composition must be communicated to the resident agent and filed with the Beneficial Ownership Registry within 30 calendar days. The annual confirmation is made by written declaration on or before June 30 and is retained by the resident agent for seven years.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400–750 per annum for resident agent and registered office services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 if not statutorily required; USD 1,500–3,500 if voluntarily engaged or required by charter
